label: <DEL> step, in sequences containing several of h/i/p/o/u/g/digits 1-3
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit. The <DEL> step holds 79% of activation mass and fires on 45% of sequences there (8.9x lift). Whether it fires at <DEL> depends on what was in the original sequence: precision rises with the number of original tokens from {h,i,p,o,u,g,1,2,3}, going 0.07 (none), 0.26 (one), 0.67 (three), 0.76 (four or more). The strongest activations are short sequences made mostly of these tokens, e.g. p 3 i h, p i i i. Sequence length on its own does not predict firing. Weaker activations (about 15% of mass) occur late in the original phase (t >= 4) on first occurrences of tokens such as w, s, e, z, k, and occasionally on the first one or two copy outputs. It never fires at t = 0 or 1, and almost never later in the copy phase. The predicate leaves out the original-phase activations, and the token-content rule is graded rather than sharp, so precision and recall stay around 0.6.
